issues.note: Primary cite does not support the claim. The back argues a larger context window fails to fix mid-input misses, but Domain-5_v2 §5.2 never mentions window size or model size at all — its only two rejected options are 'Summarize to under 20K (might lose critical information)' and 'Alternate which agent appears first (rotation doesn't fix the fundamental attention pattern)'. The second cite, §5.5, does say 'Increase the context window / switch to a larger model (cost goes up; noise problem remains)' but that is about verbose tool-output accumulation, not lost-in-the-middle. The claim actually lives in Key-Distinctions_v1 #17: 'Use a larger model with bigger context window' then 'Wrong. Larger context does not fix attention quality. More tokens available != consistent attention per token.' Exam-Mechanics_v2 Answer Pattern Heuristics repeats it: 'Attention dilution -> split passes | Inconsistent 14-file review -> per-file passes + integration pass, not a bigger context window.' Card content is correct; only the citation chain is wrong, and the first cite must be where the claim lives.

Same question, same answer as d5-045. d5-008 front: '75K-token input ... first 15K and the last 10K, but findings sitting in the middle 50K never reach its output. Which two changes address that directly?' d5-045 front: 'A synthesis step reliably uses the first and last stretches of a 75K-token input and misses findings in the middle. What two changes address the position problem?' Both backs are the §5.2 pair: key-findings summary at the start plus explicit section headings. CARD-SPEC §10: 'Do not write two cards that ask the same thing in different words.' Keep d5-045 — it carries the Key-Distinctions_v1 #20 primary cite ('Key-findings summary at the start + explicit section headings'); d5-008 cites only §5.2. NOTE FOR MERGE: killing both d5-008 and d5-010 leaves exactly six `d5.1` cards (d5-006, 007, 009, 011, 045, 046), the CARD-SPEC §7 minimum. Do not kill any further d5.1 card without writing a replacement.

Same question, same answer as d5-046. d5-010: 'Why is compress the whole 75K input to under 20K a poor response to findings being missed mid-input?' d5-046: 'Why is compressing a long input under a 20K-token ceiling the wrong answer to a middle-of-context miss?' Both backs restate Domain-5_v2 §5.2's 'Summarize to under 20K (might lose critical information)'. Keep d5-046 (cites Key-Distinctions_v1 #20 first, where the trap is catalogued: 'Summarize everything to under 20K (may lose critical information)'), after applying the trap fix filed against it.

Same answer as d5-047, in the same situation. d5-014 asks where the order ID and agreed amount should be held 'so compression cannot reach them'; d5-047 asks what structure preserves precise amounts and dates 'as a support conversation is summarized'. Both backs are the §5.4 case-facts block. Keep d5-047 — its primary cite is Key-Distinctions_v1 #21 ('Extract transactional facts into a case-facts block outside summarized history (survives compression)'), which is where the distinction is catalogued; d5-014 cites only §5.4.

This card's `trap` hands over d5-048's entire answer before Ram ever sees that card. d5-015 trap: 'raising the summarization threshold has the same defect — the numbers still get compressed, only later.' d5-048 front: 'Why does raising the summarization threshold fail to solve precision loss in a long conversation?' back: 'It postpones compression. The same transactional facts are eventually summarized into vague language anyway.' Both cards are legitimate separately (Key-Distinctions_v1 #21 lists them as two distinct wrong options: 'Revise summarization prompt to preserve numbers (still relies on perfect execution)' and 'Increase summarization threshold (buys time but doesn't fix the fundamental precision loss)'). Trim the trap so it stops answering the sibling card.

suggested.text: Exam trap: a better summarizer prompt is the tempting fix because it targets the right symptom and needs no new structure.

issues.note: Duplicates d5-050. d5-021: 'A discovery phase is filling the context window mid-task. Why is `/compact` the wrong tool here?' back: compaction removes precision later phases need, subagent keeps detail out. d5-050: 'What does a subagent give a verbose exploration that `/compact` and a split across sessions do not?' back: the verbose output never enters the main context at all. Same contrast, same source: Domain-5_v2 §5.6 'Use `/compact` mid-task (loses precision needed for implementation)'. Keep d5-050 — it cites Key-Distinctions_v1 #22 as well and covers the `--continue` option too.

Duplicates d5-052. d5-022: 'A book club thread has run three months and 85K tokens. A member asks what the group concluded about a specific theme discussed weeks ago. Which memory design answers that?' d5-052: 'Someone asks what a group concluded about one theme eleven weeks and 85K tokens ago. Which memory strategy answers it?' Identical back (semantic retrieval / embeddings over full history), identical source scenario in Domain-5_v2 §5.7. Keep d5-052 — its primary cite is Key-Distinctions_v1 #24, where the distinction is catalogued.

Two questions in one front — 'What is this, and what stops it?' — producing a two-part back ('Context degradation — write intermediate findings to a scratchpad file and read it back at the start of each continuation'). CARD-SPEC §1: 'If the front invites an essay, split it into two cards.' Both halves are supported by Domain-5_v2 §5.12 ('counteracts context degradation, where the model starts giving inconsistent answers and referencing typical patterns instead of the specific classes it discovered earlier'), so this is a shape defect, not a fact defect. Narrow the front to the remedy and let the name of the failure sit in the back.

suggested.text: Deep into a long investigation the model starts citing typical patterns instead of the specific classes it found earlier. What mechanism holds the specifics?

issues.note: The trap asserts an option the corpus does not put in this scenario: 'Exam trap: a larger context window is offered too.' Domain-5_v2 §5.2's option list for the 75K synthesis scenario is only 'Summarize to under 20K' and 'Alternate which agent appears first', and Key-Distinctions_v1 #20 lists the same two. The larger-window rejection is real corpus material but belongs to Key-Distinctions_v1 #17 and to §5.5's tool-output scenario — it is not a documented distractor here, and d5-007 already drills it. CARD-SPEC §10: 'If the corpus does not say it, it does not go on a card.' Keep the second sentence, which is accurate and load-bearing.

suggested.text: Exam trap: lost-in-the-middle is a positional attention pattern rather than a capacity limit, so shrinking the input does not move the finding out of the middle.

issues.note: Thinner restatement of d5-020. d5-020: '120-file codebase in three phases ... Phase 1 discovery floods the main context window ... What structure fixes it?' back: Explore subagent, returns a summary, phases 2 and 3 continue in the main conversation. d5-049: 'A discovery phase across a 120-file codebase fills the window before implementation even begins. What isolates it?' back: 'An Explore subagent runs the verbose discovery and returns a concise summary.' Same scenario (Domain-5_v2 §5.6), same answer. Keep d5-020, which carries the `--continue` distractor in its trap; Key-Distinctions_v1 #22 remains cited by d5-050.

The trap demotes a mitigation the corpus endorses. Domain-5_v2 §5.13 lists three 'Preventive patterns' with no ranking among them: 'Inject reminder messages at conversation breakpoints (reinforcement)', 'Keep system prompt rules concrete and minimal', 'Replace verbose rule lists with few-shot examples'. §5.14 pairs them as one solution: 'Inject reminders at breakpoints; use few-shot over verbose rules.' This card's trap says reminder injection 'addresses the symptom while leaving the abstractness that drifts fastest in place' — that ranking is not in the corpus, and it contradicts d5-041 in the same deck, whose back teaches both fixes together ('Inject reminder messages at conversation breakpoints, and replace verbose rule lists with few-shot examples'). Drilled as written, it would train Ram to reject a correct option.

suggested.text: Exam trap: adding more explicit rules to a prompt that is already failing does not help — the corpus fix is examples, not more instruction text.

issues.note: Collides with two cards at once. Its stem ('A three-turn conversation loses what the user said in turn 1') is d5-001's stem; its answer ('include the prior messages in the `messages` array. Vector retrieval is for recall across months of history') is d5-003's answer. All three trace to the same Domain-5_v2 §5.1 scenario and Key-Distinctions_v1 #25. Keep d5-001 (the root-cause card) and d5-003 (the vector-DB card, whose back draws the within-session vs cross-session boundary more precisely). Note: Key-Distinctions_v1 #25 stays cited by d5-054, so no cite coverage is lost.

This card is d5-017 and d5-018 recombined. Its back ('A `PostToolUse` hook that trims the result to the relevant fields before it enters context') is d5-017's back; its trap ('instructing the model to ignore the irrelevant fields still pays for every one of those tokens') is d5-018's whole card. All three cite Domain-5_v2 §5.5 only. Keep d5-017 (the crisp hook-name fact) and d5-018 (the ignore-the-fields trap).

Compound front that re-asks three existing cards: 'Which escalation triggers are reliable, and which two proxies does the exam reject outright?' The reliable-triggers half is d5-024, the sentiment half is d5-025, the self-confidence half is d5-026 — all citing Domain-5_v2 §5.8. CARD-SPEC §1 also rules against the shape: 'could Ram answer the front out loud in under ten seconds' — this one needs a list of five triggers plus two rejected proxies.

The deck carries four `d5.2` caching cards (d5-043, d5-044, d5-058, d5-059). CARD-SPEC §7 caps it: 'So write two cards at most, and write them about that: caching is out of scope past knowing it exists, and use prompt caching to cut cost is a distractor shape.' d5-058 is the scope card duplicated — d5-043 front: 'How far into prompt caching does CCA-F scope reach?' d5-058 front: 'How much prompt caching does the CCA-F expect you to know?' Same answer from the same line, Exam-Mechanics_v2 Out-of-Scope Topics: 'Prompt caching implementation details (beyond knowing it exists)'. Keep d5-043.

Secondary defect if it were kept: the back adds 'and when it pays', which the cited out-of-scope line does not say — that phrasing comes from CARD-SPEC §10, not from the corpus. d5-043's back stays inside what the cite supports.

The fourth `d5.2` card, over the CARD-SPEC §7 two-card cap, and a duplicate of d5-044: both fronts are 'an option proposes prompt caching to cut cost' and both backs resolve to over-engineering. Keep d5-044, whose back is anchored in a heuristic the cite actually contains.

The back makes a claim its cites do not carry: 'As a wrong answer: an over-engineered cost fix' — described as how caching behaves 'in the official samples'. Exam-Mechanics_v2 Answer Pattern Heuristics is a table of twelve heuristics ('Proportionate first response | Try the prompt/description fix before adding infrastructure') and never mentions caching; Out-of-Scope Topics only says implementation details will not appear. The 'appears only as a wrong option in the official samples' statement lives in CARD-SPEC §7, which is a spec, not a citable corpus file.

Overlaps d5-031 on the same sentence of Domain-5_v2 §5.9: 'An aggregate 97% accuracy can hide a 40% failure rate on one rare document type.' d5-031 already states the 40% figure inside its own back ('an aggregate figure can hide a rare document type failing 40% of the time'), so d5-061's front asks for something d5-031 has already handed over. d5-061's distinct value is in its trap (auditing only the low-confidence queue, sampling only the common document type — both documented as wrong in §5.9). Repoint the front at that, so the two cards stop competing.

suggested.text: Which two sampling shortcuts leave the failing segment of an extraction pipeline unmeasured?
